doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Maynard Ferguson and Dizzy's big band
title: Starving and practicing in a one-room kitchenette with Hubbard
summary: Hampton shared a room across from the Apollo with Freddie Hubbard, Floyd Brady and Rocky Boyd, hungry but practicing.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How many nights a week were you working?
Sometimes we weren’t working at all, because we were new. So we were there living – Freddie Hubbard, myself, and two other guys in a room. We weren’t working at all. We practiced all the time.
This is the same room that you walked out of when you met Charlie Parker?
Yeah.
Where you lived with that group of musicians?
Yeah.
Give us that address, if you recall.
I don’t remember the address, but it was just across from the back of the Apollo Theater. That building’s gone now. I had a one-room kitchenette. One bed. We slept all in the same bed.
Give us this quartet again.

It was Freddie Hubbard. Another man. His name was Floyd Brady. He played trombone – played beautiful trombone. We were there in the room together all the time. I’m writing. He’s playing. I have to stop writing, the guy’s playing so beautiful. I got him a job with Buddy Johnson. Then there was a saxophone player, Rocky Boyd. We were all living together. We didn’t have any money. We didn’t have any food. We just practiced all the time.
What’d you eat?
We ate some stuff that nobody should eat.
Spam?
No. Wish we could have had some Spam. Spam would have been like lamb chops. A can of Spam – that would have been like a Thanksgiving dinner.
How long did this go on?
We were there for a couple of months like that.
You didn’t want to go back to Indianapolis?
Oh no, no. I was . . .
Pride?
No, no. I was in music. I didn’t care. We were playing music. They didn’t have to give no food, didn’t have to be no food around. We were – whenever we had a chance to play music, we did it.
Was this prior to starting to work with the Lionel Hamptons and the Maynard Fergusons?
That was prior to that, yeah.
Okay. So this is, say, between ’52 and ’56.
It was after Buddy.
Things were hard for a minute.
I didn’t feel it was hard, but we didn’t have anything to eat. There was water. Didn’t have to pay for that. We could do that.
